title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, timeouts
author: Ava Chen
body: Motivation: Production traffic showed occasional starvation of low-latency requests when the continuous batcher aggressively aggregated requests for throughput. This PR tunes the scheduler to balance queueing efficiency with fairness so short-latency-critical requests are not delayed behind large batches. Changes: 1) Introduce per-priority queueing windows and max-wait timeouts to prevent indefinite starvation of higher-priority small requests. 2) Make scheduler heuristics aware of request size distribution; prefer forming small 'fast-path' batches when the proportion of short sequences exceeds a threshold. 3) Add jittered backoff for long-wait requests to avoid synchronized wakeups and thundering-batch effects. 4) Add fairness token bucket overlay to ensure each priority class receives a minimum fraction of service over time. 5) Expose tuning knobs via continuous_batcher/config.rs and add runtime metrics (scheduler_wait_time_{p50,p95,p99}, starvation_count, fast_path_hits) for visibility. Backwards compatibility: default settings are conservative and preserve current throughput-focused behavior unless operators opt-in to more aggressive fairness guarantees. Checklist: - [x] Design doc and matching Linear tickets referenced (ENG-3421, ENG-3478) - [x] Unit tests for scheduler state transitions - [x] Integration tests with simulated mixed-size traffic - [x] Benchmark harness with p50/p95/p99 and throughput numbers - [x] Observability added to Console dashboards Changeset summary (commits listed below) and high-level files changed: runtime/continuous_batcher/scheduler.rs (core scheduler logic, ~260 additions/60 deletions), runtime/continuous_batcher/queue.rs (per-priority queueing window logic, ~80 additions/20 deletions), runtime/continuous_batcher/config.rs (expose knobs), runtime/continuous_batcher/metrics.rs (new metrics), runtime/continuous_batcher/tests/scheduler_tests.rs (new unit tests), benchmarks/continuous-batcher/fairness_bench.toml (bench config), docs/running/continuous-batcher.md (runtime tuning guidance). Testing and results: - Unit tests: added 24 tests covering queueing windows, timeout expiry, and token-bucket fairness overlay. All pass locally and on CI. - Integration: simulated mixed-traffic (30% short requests, 70% long) on 4xA100 nodes; observed p99 latency reduction for short requests from 420ms -> 360ms (14% improvement) while overall throughput reduced by ~2% at peak. - Starvation prevention: synthetic workload that previously produced starvation events now shows zero starvation events during a 10m run. - Benchmarks: included reproducible bench config; CI runs report baseline vs tuned results. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag continuous_batcher.fairness.enabled (disabled by default for a canary rollout), gradual ramp to 100% with monitoring alerts for throughput regression >5% or p99 increase >10%. Notes: tuned defaults chosen after a sweep of parameters (window_ms in [5,20,50], max_wait_ms in [10,50,200], fairness_token_rate in [0.05,0.2]). Documentation: added section to continuous-batcher README with recommended settings for latency-sensitive vs throughput-sensitive workloads.

review_comments: Raj Patel: Can you explain why we picked a 50ms default window? Will this hurt very short sequences?

Ava Chen: The 50ms default was chosen after the parameter sweep; it balances throughput and p99 for our typical mix. We expose window_ms and max_wait_ms in config for operators to tune; the doc has guidance for < 20ms for very latency-sensitive workloads.
Elena Morales: Please add metrics to observe starvation_count per priority and add alerts for >0 during canary. Also include a dashboard tile in Console.

Ava Chen: Added starvation_count and fast_path_hits metrics; docs updated with dashboard instructions. Alert suggestion added to ci/alerts/continuous-batcher-alerts.yaml (separate PR will wire alerts).
Tom Briggs: I saw a flake in CI where a test intermittently failed due to queue wakeup ordering. Can we add deterministic ordering and a unit test?
Ava Chen: Found a race in the wakeup path; fixed ordering and added unit to cover the scenario (commit 8f3b2c1). CI was rerun and passes.
ci_checks: Benchmarks: reported - baseline vs tuned (attached artifacts)
benchmarks_summary: Mixed-traffic 4xA100: short request p99 improved 420ms -> 360ms (~14%), p95 improved 180ms -> 150ms (~17%), overall throughput -2% at peak. Starvation events reduced from 12/10m -> 0/10m in synthetic replay.
release_notes: Improve continuous-batcher scheduler to reduce starvation and improve fairness across priority classes. Adds new tuning knobs and metrics. Default behavior unchanged; opt-in fairness flag available for canary rollout.
